title: FileOutputStream closes when receiving debug stderr logging from rsandbox
description:
The SageMaker team ran into an issue where output streams would intermittently fail to open for some jobs. Upon diagnosis, in these cases there was some debug `stderr` logging coming from `rsandbox` for the `tail` process launched by the output stream to read the job's output files. The offending code is:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/6c676dd10dc7b09a0635c630454922c8f9d212a9/sdk/src/api/stream/FileOutputStream.cpp#L326-L347

As can be seen, if any `stderr` is received, we fail the stream and clean it up by calling `reportError`. However, there is no need to do this at all, as any legitimate error will end in the process exiting, and the stream will get cleaned up properly in the exit callback. Instead, we should _only_ log in this case when receiving `stderr` for the launched `tail` (and `rsandbox`).

title: Plugin cannot properly drop privilege twice, causing fatal error
description:
Currently, the SageMaker plugin SDK cannot properly start without a code patch to the SDK. The following is the error they get:

```
2022-06-28T16:29:02.737432Z [rstudio-sagemaker-launcher] INFO Received signal: 2
2022-06-28T16:29:02.737790Z [rstudio-sagemaker-launcher] INFO Stopping plugin...
2022-06-28T16:29:56.703204Z [rstudio-sagemaker-launcher] ERROR SystemError error 1 (Operation not permitted) [subcategory: system]; OCCURRED AT temporarilyDropPrivileges /local/home/jedambr/RStudioUpdate2022/src/Rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/third-party-src/sdk/src/system/PosixSystem.cpp:262
2022-06-28T16:29:56.703568Z [rstudio-sagemaker-launcher] ERROR Could not lower privilege to server user: sagemaker-user.
```

Possible causes:

1. Early during startup, we check the scratch path and drop privileges from root -> server user. This also was how things worked before the new SDK release: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/b0b55f44dbd09254ab9dc4afc781101d96bb3087/sdk/src/AbstractMain.cpp#L92-L94
2. In the new version, in addition, we need to setup the file log destination with root privileges to ensure we can initially create the file under /var/log. We restore root https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/b0b55f44dbd09254ab9dc4afc781101d96bb3087/sdk/src/AbstractMain.cpp#L221-L226
3. After we're done with setting up the log file, we again lower root privilege in the new version: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/b0b55f44dbd09254ab9dc4afc781101d96bb3087/sdk/src/AbstractMain.cpp#L244-L250

From the SageMaker logs, it looks like maybe the call to `restoreRoot` is not allowing them to again call `temporarilyDropPrivileges` again. In the previous version, there was one `restoreRoot() -> temporarilyDropPrivileges()` call. In the new version, there are two.

SageMaker is working around the issue by commenting out the following code in `AbstractMain.cpp`: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/6c676dd10dc7b09a0635c630454922c8f9d212a9/sdk/src/AbstractMain.cpp#L244-L250

title: Long running jobs are pruned while running on Launcher restart
description:
1. Start a job that runs for longer than the `job-expiry-hours` prune interval (e.g. 28 hours)
2. While the job is still running, restart the Launcher SDK plugin
3. Upon start, the following code is run to ensure that loaded jobs that should be are pruned from the system. https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/6c676dd10dc7b09a0635c630454922c8f9d212a9/sdk/src/jobs/AbstractJobRepository.cpp#L135-L152 The function that prunes the startup jobs is: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/6c676dd10dc7b09a0635c630454922c8f9d212a9/sdk/src/jobs/JobPruner.cpp#L82-L117
4. Jobs that are still in the RUNNING state are pruned INCORRECTLY if they should be pruned due to expiry. The job status is not correctly checked here.

The fix is to ensure that the job is only removed/pruned if the job has actually completed. We need an extra check for `job->isCompleted()` here: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/6c676dd10dc7b09a0635c630454922c8f9d212a9/sdk/src/jobs/JobPruner.cpp#L82-L99

title: Eliminate Manual Copy Steps for Making Documentation Live
description:
When releasing a new version of the SDK, the documentation is uploaded to the following places:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/b0b55f44dbd09254ab9dc4afc781101d96bb3087/Jenkinsfile#L81-L89

However, our official documentation points to the root of the buckets, as seen in the path here: https://docs.rstudio.com/rlps/quickstart/. Note that it points to the root of the `quickstart` bucket, not `quickstart/latest`. This is linked to here: https://www.rstudio.com/products/launcher-plugin-sdk/

We should either adjust the release steps to automatically copy to the root of the bucket as well, or adjust the links to point to the `/latest` path. We only want this to happen when we make the new version of the SDK live, so this might necessitate a new release pipeline.

title: Move steps in `pull-shared-core.sh` to language with proper regex support
description:
The current process of creating a new SDK release process pulls in the [`shared_core`](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/tree/main/src/cpp/shared_core) library from the rstudio repo. Various modifications are made to these files using regexes and `sed`.

It would be beneficial to move this into a language that has full regex support as part of its standard library. This will allow modification of the files in memory as well as having the following additional benefits:
* Named match groups in regex patterns
* Multi-line regexes
* lookahead/lookbehind assertions
* Saving compiled regex to variables
* Combining already-defined regexes into more complex patterns

This should result in more flexibility as well as improved readability and maintainability.

title: Docs: Add More Details About Reporting Support for Containers
description:
There are currently instructions about when you should report support for containers, but not about why you should report support for containers. We should document the different behaviour that consumers of the Launcher will have when working with Plugins that support containers. Non-exhaustive list below:

* The consumer will set the ExposedPorts object on the Job, telling the plugin which ports it needs exposed to communicate with the Job.
* The consumer may modify how the Job is launched to account for container limitations. For example:
  * the IDE can be configured to create container users when the job starts. 
  * the IDE can be configured to forward the current environment to the container
  * the IDE will disable project sharing in a containerized job context
  * the IDE will bind the session to a specific port, for the purposes of exposing the port
  * the IDE will enable proxying shiny apps through the R session so they still work without exposing more ports
  * the IDE can be configured to request that the container run as the root user
  * the IDE will disable project sharing in R sessions

title: Docs: Add instructions for the ExposedPorts Feature
description: The sample Local Plugin does not make use of the ExposedPorts feature, and the QuickStart guide does not cover it. We should add an AdvancedFeature section to explain how to make use of this feature.

title: Docs: Add instructions to configure the Launcher to start a Plugin
description:
We should include in the QuickStart or the Dev Guide how to configure the Launcher to load the Plugin. Specifically, add the following to `/etc/rstudio/launcher.conf`:

```ini
[cluster]
name=MyPlugin
type=MyPlugin
exe=/path/to/plugin/executable
```

title: Change subprocess exit code detection to return 128 + signal
description:
We recently made a change in the upstream RSP code to report process exit codes as 128+signal if the process exited due to a signal. This is a bash paradigm that is fairly widely recognized.

Update the SDK subprocess exit code detection mechanism similarly to what was done for https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/2045.

title: Docs: Missing instruction to update exe name
description: Plugin developers will need to change the quickstart executable name from `rstudio-quickstart-launcher` to `myorg-myplugin-launcher`. This is not currently documented anywhere. Add this instruction to the quickstart guide.

title: FileOutputStream retry period
description:
If the job is running but the output files haven't been created yet, we exit the stream immediately. We should give the output files a grace period to be created, and make the value configurable.

Since not every plugin will use FileOutputStream, the configurable-ness of the grace period time needs to be on a per-plugin basis.

title: Ensure latest group data is retrieved
description: Currently the SDK will populate group members once, on initialisation of `AbstractUserProfiles`. This means Plugins will have to be restarted when a member is added to a group. We can fix this by fetching the set of members each time a value is requested.

title: Local Launcher Load Balancing Support
description:
Implement load balancing support for the SDK-based Local Launcher, per the existing implementation.

Requires `NodeManager` or equivalent. The root directory for writing information is `<scratch-path>/[jobs|output]/<hostname>` . 

The plugin is already writing output and job information to the correct location. It should also write network information to the `<scratch-path>/jobs/<hostname>/addrs` file. It should read additional node network information from the same file for different hostnames.

The plugin needs to use the network information to pull request information from the other Local Plugin nodes in the load balanced cluster.

title: Process tests cannot run in Jenkins without `rsandbox`
description: The process launching unit tests require `rsandbox` to pass. We should modify the test environment to include `rsandbox` and re-enable the process tests.

title: Remove manual effort in updating shared_core
description:
Currently when updating components that come from shared_core, there are a few changes I've made manually that I have to discard before committing. As of May 23, 2020, these manual discards include:

* `+#include <boost/current_function.hpp>` and `+#include <boost/system/error_code.hpp>` in `Error.hpp`
* `Error`  constructors and operators which accept `boost::system::error_code` or `boost::system::error_condition` in `Error.hpp` and `Error.cpp`.
* The modified macro definitions in `Error.hpp` which would rely boost.
* Anything which is in an `#ifdef _WIN32` block in any file.
* `+#ifndef _WIN32` and closing `+#endif` lines in any file.
* `+#out_values = boost::none;` in `Json.cpp`.
* The modification of `#include <boost/noncopyable.hpp>` to `#include <Noncopyable.hpp>` 
* The duplication of `namespace system {` in `FilePath.hpp` (this may be a bug in [pull-shared-core.sh script](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-launcher-plugin-sdk/blob/master/tools/pull-shared-core.sh)) and it's accompanying `} // namespace system` line.
* `+#include <boost/utility.hpp>` and `-#include <Noncopyable>` in `FilePath.hpp`.
* `+bool isJunction() const;` in `FilePath.hpp`, and accompanying comments.
* `-#include <boost/system/error_code.hpp>` in `Error.cpp`
* The modified style of error creation in the `systemError` functions in `Error.cpp`.
* `-#include <utils/ErrorUtils.hpp>` in `Json.cpp`
* The modified `Json(?:Pointer)?ParseErrorCategory` name fields in `Json.cpp`
* The modification to use `utils::createErrorFromBoostError` instead of the `Error` constructor directly in any file.
* `-#include <mutex>` and `+#include <boost/thread.hpp>` in `FileLogDestination.cpp`.
* `-#include <boost/algorithm/string.hpp>` and `+#include <Optional.hpp>` in `Logger.cpp`
* The corrected alphabetization of includes in `Logger.cpp` (this really should be fixed on the IDE side, and it would go away on its own).
* The modified conversion from time to `string` in `Logger.cpp`.
* The different style of static initialization of the `static Logger` value in `Logger.cpp`. (We may later want to adopt this change if we find there are issues with writing to the logger after static destruction).
* `-#include <utils/ErrorUtils.hpp>` in `FilePath.cpp`.
* The removal of `#ifdef __APPLE__` blocks and `+#ifndef __APPLE__` with accompanying `+#endif` in any file.
* The addition of `getEnvironmentVariable` in `PosixSystem.hpp` and `PosixSystem.cpp`, as well as the removal of `getEnvVariable` in `User.cpp` and the modified calls. (This change should be added in the IDE to resolve the conflict).
* The modified error type and log call in the definition of `RW_LOCK_END` in `ReaderWriterMutex.hpp`.

I propose editing the list to cross out items as they are resolved.
